experiences.name: Xel-Ha Eco Water Park

experiences.location: Xel-Ha, Riviera Maya, 75 km south of Cancun

experiences.location: Playa Langosta area, Zona Hotelera, Cancun

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cancun
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.description: Visit Cancun's most iconic public beach at sunrise for stunning views of the Caribbean Sea. day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on flight AA. Clear customs and immigration, collect baggage, and arrange budget-friendly transportation to Cancun Beach Resort (take the ADO public bus from the airport for around $10 USD instead of a taxi to save money). Check in or drop off luggage if room isn't ready.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a short walk to the nearest public beach stretch along the Hotel Zone. Relax on the sand, take a dip in the turquoise Caribbean Sea, and get oriented with the surroundings. Explore the beachfront area on foot and enjoy the views without spending anything.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Playa Langosta area and enjoy dinner at El Fish Fritanga for an authentic and affordable local seafood experience. Try their fried fish platters or shrimp tacos at budget-friendly prices. Afterward, take a leisurely evening stroll along the beachfront boulevard.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or light meal at the airport before or after landing — look for a OXXO convenience store or airport café for a quick and cheap bite (around $5 USD).
meals.lunch: Pick up affordable street tacos or a torta from a local taqueria near the hotel zone for $3–6 USD.
meals.dinner: El Fish Fritanga near Playa Langosta — budget-friendly seafood plates ranging from $8–15 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light since you arrive at 11 AM. Focus on getting settled and acclimating. Buy a local SIM card at the airport (Telcel or AT&T Mexico) for around $10–15 USD to save on roaming charges throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and head to Playa Delfines for a stunning sunrise over the Caribbean Sea. This is Cancun's most iconic and completely free public beach. Arrive around 6:00–6:30 AM to catch the best light. Bring water and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere before the crowds arrive. Take photos at the famous 'CANCUN' sign.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a late breakfast, then spend the afternoon at the hotel beach or nearby public beach. Rent a snorkel set from a local beach vendor (around $10 USD) and explore the shallow reef areas near the shore. Alternatively, walk along the Hotel Zone boulevard and browse the free views and scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple meal or grab groceries from a nearby Walmart Supercenter or Chedraui supermarket in the Hotel Zone to stock up on snacks, water, and easy meals for the room. Spend the evening relaxing on the beach watching the sunset.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a local comedor or market near the hotel — look for a set breakfast (huevos rancheros, juice, coffee) for around $4–7 USD.
meals.lunch: Buy fresh fruit, bread, and snacks from a local market or OXXO for a budget beach picnic ($3–5 USD).
meals.dinner: Cook in-room with supermarket groceries or grab affordable tacos from a street vendor near the hotel zone ($5–8 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Playa Delfines is accessible by the free city bus (Ruta 1) that runs along Boulevard Kukulcan in the Hotel Zone — a great way to save on transportation. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water for the beach day.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning exploring Playa Tortugas and Playa Caracol, two free public beaches in the northern Hotel Zone. These beaches are calmer and great for swimming. Arrive early to claim a good spot on the sand. Enjoy the warm Caribbean water and relax.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the public bus to Mercado 28 (downtown Cancun) — a vibrant local market where you can browse handmade crafts, souvenirs, and authentic Mexican goods at negotiable prices. Practice your bargaining skills! This is one of the most budget-friendly shopping experiences in Cancun.
day_by_day.evening: Explore downtown Cancun (El Centro) for dinner at one of the many affordable local restaurants around Parque de las Palapas. This central park often has free live music and cultural events in the evening. Enjoy the local atmosphere away from the touristy Hotel Zone.

meals.breakfast: Grab a budget breakfast at a local bakery (panadería) near the hotel — fresh pan dulce, coffee, and juice for $3–5 USD.
meals.lunch: Eat at Mercado 28's food court — authentic cochinita pibil, salbutes, or panuchos for $4–7 USD per person.
meals.dinner: Parque de las Palapas area restaurants offer full meals for $6–10 USD. Try a local Mexican restaurant for enchiladas, tamales, or fresh seafood soup.

day_by_day.notes: The public bus (R-1 or R-2) runs frequently between the Hotel Zone and downtown Cancun for about $0.50–1 USD each way — extremely budget-friendly. Downtown Cancun gives you a much more authentic Mexican experience away from tourist prices.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to Isla Mujeres via the public ferry from Puerto Juarez (much cheaper than the Hotel Zone ferry — around $5–7 USD round trip). Arrive early and rent a golf cart or bicycle to explore the small island. Visit Playa Norte, consistently rated one of the most beautiful beaches in the Caribbean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Isla Mujeres — walk to the southern tip to see the cliffs and the small Mayan ruins of the Ixchel Temple. Swim in the crystal-clear shallow waters of Playa Norte and enjoy the laid-back island vibe. The entire island is walkable or easily explored by bicycle.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun via the ferry before sunset. Grab dinner at a local seafood spot near the hotel zone or pick up street food on the way back. Relax at the hotel and prepare for the next day.

meals.breakfast: Eat a quick breakfast at the hotel or grab something from OXXO before catching the ferry ($3–5 USD).
meals.lunch: On Isla Mujeres, eat at one of the local comedores on the main street away from the tourist waterfront — fish tacos, ceviche, or a full comida corrida for $6–10 USD.
meals.dinner: Street tacos or a local taqueria near the hotel on return to Cancun ($5–8 USD).

day_by_day.notes: To get to Puerto Juarez ferry terminal cheaply, take the public bus from the Hotel Zone (R-1) toward downtown and then a taxi or another bus to Puerto Juarez. Total transportation cost is significantly lower than taking the Hotel Zone ferry. Bring cash, sunscreen, and a reusable water bottle.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Playa Delfines for a morning swim and beach relaxation — this time enjoy it in full daylight. Walk along the beach and collect shells. The beach has free parking and public facilities. Bring a book and enjoy a slow, relaxing morning by the sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Cancun Underwater Museum (MUSA) viewpoint from the surface — you can see some of the submerged sculptures from glass-bottom boat tours at budget prices (around $20–25 USD) rather than paying for a full diving experience. Alternatively, spend the afternoon at Playa Ballenas, another free public beach with calmer waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to El Fish Fritanga for a final seafood dinner, or explore other affordable beachside eateries near Playa Langosta. Afterward, enjoy a final sunset walk along the beach boulevard and pick up any last souvenirs from local vendors.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple breakfast with groceries from the supermarket in the room ($2–4 USD).
meals.lunch: Beach picnic with groceries from the supermarket — sandwiches, fruit, chips, and drinks ($4–6 USD).
meals.dinner: El Fish Fritanga or a nearby local seafood restaurant ($8–15 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Friday evenings in the Hotel Zone can get lively — enjoy the atmosphere but be mindful of budget. Street vendors along the boulevard often sell fresh coconuts and snacks at very reasonable prices. A fresh coconut on the beach is one of Cancun's best budget treats at $2–3 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely morning at the hotel beach. Take one last swim in the Caribbean Sea and soak up the sun. Pack your bags and do a final check of the room. Check out of the hotel and store luggage at the front desk if your flight is later in the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, take a final stroll through the Hotel Zone or grab any last-minute snacks and souvenirs from local vendors. Head to the airport via the ADO public bus (around $10 USD) to save money on the return transfer.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Cancun with wonderful beach memories and a wallet that survived the trip. Review your budget savings and reflect on the incredible experiences had throughout the week.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at a local café or with remaining room groceries ($4–7 USD).
meals.lunch: Grab a light meal near the hotel zone or at the airport — OXXO snacks or a quick local restaurant before heading to the airport ($5–8 USD).
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight meal depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Keep your ADO bus ticket or confirm the bus schedule the night before to ensure a smooth, budget-friendly airport transfer. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before your international flight. Total estimated daily budget per person: $40–60 USD including food, transport, and activities.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on flight AA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange airport transfer to Cancun Beach Resort. Check-in and get settled into your room (early check-in subject to availability). Freshen up and orient yourself with the resort amenities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely first stroll along the Hotel Zone (Zona Hotelera) beach strip near the resort. Dip your toes in the turquoise Caribbean Sea, relax on the beach, and soak in the stunning scenery. Visit a nearby convenience store or resort shop to grab any essentials for the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the resort's beachfront restaurant or a nearby mid-range spot in the Hotel Zone. Stroll along Boulevard Kukulcan after dinner to get your bearings and enjoy the lively atmosphere of the strip.

meals.breakfast: Grab a bite at the airport or a quick snack upon arrival at the resort
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at the resort pool bar or beach snack stand — try fish tacos or a fresh ceviche
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Destilería or a similar mid-range Mexican restaurant in the Hotel Zone (~$20–35 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Since arrival is at 11:00 AM, keep Day 1 light and low-key. Confirm check-in time with Cancun Beach Resort in advance. Exchange some currency or withdraw pesos from an airport ATM for smaller purchases throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for the Playa Delfines Sunrise Visit. Head to Cancun's most iconic public beach before dawn to witness a breathtaking Caribbean sunrise. Bring a camera and enjoy the quiet, crowd-free atmosphere. The famous 'CANCUN' sign makes for a great photo opportunity. Return to the resort for a proper breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Punta Nizuc for a Snorkeling at Punta Nizuc Reef experience. Join a guided snorkeling tour to explore the vibrant coral reef, part of the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef System. Spot colorful tropical fish, sea turtles, and stunning coral formations in crystal-clear waters. Tours typically last 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort to rinse off and relax. Head out for dinner at a local seafood spot in the Hotel Zone. Enjoy the warm evening breeze with a cocktail on a rooftop bar afterward.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at the resort or a nearby café — eggs, fresh tropical fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beachside palapa near Punta Nizuc or pack snacks for the snorkeling tour
meals.dinner: Beachside Seafood Dining at El Fish Fritanga near Playa Langosta — try grilled whole fish or shrimp tacos (~$15–25 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Punta Nizuc snorkeling tour in advance online or through the resort concierge. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a towel, and water shoes. Playa Delfines is accessible by the free Hotel Zone public bus (R-1).

day_by_day.morning: Full-day adventure at Xel-Ha Eco Water Park. Depart early from the resort (approximately 1.5 hours south toward Tulum). Spend the morning snorkeling in the natural coastal lagoon, floating down lazy rivers, and exploring mangrove trails. The all-inclusive entry covers food, drinks, and equipment rentals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying Xel-Ha in the afternoon — try the cliff jump, rent a bike to explore the park's pathways, or relax in a hammock over the water. Take advantage of the all-inclusive dining options within the park for lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun by early evening (shuttle or rental car). Enjoy a quiet dinner near the resort and an early night to recover from the full day of activity.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — pack a light snack for the road
meals.lunch: All-inclusive lunch inside Xel-Ha park — buffet with Mexican dishes, grilled meats, and fresh juices
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at a mid-range restaurant near the resort, such as Ty-Coz or a local taqueria (~$12–20 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Xel-Ha all-inclusive tickets are approximately $100–130 USD per person — book online in advance for discounts. Wear your swimsuit under your clothes for easy access. The park opens at 8:30 AM; arrive early to make the most of your day. Transportation can be arranged through the resort or booked as part of a tour package.

day_by_day.morning: Take the ferry from Puerto Juárez or Gran Puerto terminal for the Isla Mujeres Day Trip. The ferry ride takes about 20–30 minutes. Arrive on the charming island and rent a golf cart to explore — visit the colorful streets, the Turtle Farm (Tortugranja), and the scenic Punta Sur cliffs at the southern tip of the island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the world-famous Playa Norte, consistently rated one of the best beaches in the world. Swim in the calm, shallow turquoise waters, rent a beach chair and umbrella, and enjoy the laid-back island vibe. Browse the local artisan shops along Hidalgo Street.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the last ferry back to Cancun (ferries run until around 11:30 PM). Enjoy a relaxed dinner back in the Hotel Zone or at a restaurant near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before heading to the ferry terminal
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beachfront restaurant on Isla Mujeres — try the grilled lobster or fish of the day at Lancheros or Playa Norte beach bar (~$15–25 USD per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range Hotel Zone restaurant — try Labná for traditional Yucatecan cuisine (~$20–30 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ferry tickets cost approximately $10–15 USD round trip per person. Golf cart rentals on Isla Mujeres run about $40–50 USD for the day. Bring cash as some vendors on the island are cash-only. Apply sunscreen generously — the island has very little shade on the beach.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a free morning at the resort beach. Sleep in, order room service or enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast, and spend time relaxing by the pool or ocean. This is your recovery and leisure day — read a book, take a swim, or book a resort spa treatment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mercado 28 (Market 28) in downtown Cancun for authentic local shopping — pick up handcrafted souvenirs, hammocks, jewelry, and local snacks. Bargaining is expected and encouraged. Alternatively, browse the La Isla Shopping Village mall in the Hotel Zone for a mix of international and Mexican brands.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your last full evening with a memorable beachfront dinner. Return to El Fish Fritanga or try a new upscale-casual seafood restaurant. After dinner, enjoy sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar such as Mandala Beach Club or a similar venue along the Hotel Zone strip.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent resort breakfast — fresh fruit, omelets, pastries, and tropical juices
meals.lunch: Street food lunch near Mercado 28 — try cochinita pibil tacos, elotes, and agua fresca (~$5–10 USD per person)
meals.dinner: Celebratory seafood dinner at a beachfront restaurant — grilled lobster, shrimp, or the catch of the day (~$30–45 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Mercado 28 is located in downtown Cancun — take a taxi or the public bus (Route 1) from the Hotel Zone. Budget about $30–60 USD for souvenirs. If booking a spa treatment at the resort, reserve it in advance as slots fill quickly on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one final sunrise walk along the hotel zone beach. Pack your bags and complete checkout formalities. Enjoy a last breakfast at the resort, savoring the views of the Caribbean one more time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, squeeze in a final activity — a quick dip at the nearest beach, a last round of fresh coconut water from a beachside vendor, or a final souvenir run. Arrange airport transfer through the resort concierge or a pre-booked taxi.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Cancun International Airport with plenty of time before your departure. Reflect on an incredible 6-day Cancun adventure filled with beaches, reefs, islands, and authentic Mexican culture.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — enjoy a full sit-down meal before checkout
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a quick stop at a nearby café before departure
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your international flight for airport check-in and security. Confirm your departure terminal in advance. Keep some pesos handy for tips, last-minute snacks, or airport purchases. Declare any goods purchased in Mexico as required by customs regulations.

day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into resort life with an afternoon at the hotel's premium beach club. Enjoy a reserved beachfront cabana with personalized butler service, refreshing cocktails, and the turquoise Caribbean waters at your doorstep. Take a dip in the sea or the resort's infinity pool.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed first-night dinner at the resort's signature fine dining restaurant. Savor fresh seafood and regional Mexican cuisine paired with premium wines while overlooking the illuminated Caribbean Sea.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport lounge before landing
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at the resort's beachside grill — grilled lobster tacos, ceviche, and fresh tropical juices
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — multi-course tasting menu featuring Yucatecan-inspired cuisine with sommelier-selected wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in in advance to ensure your suite is ready upon arrival. Ask the concierge to arrange a beachfront cabana for the afternoon. Keep the evening light as jet lag or travel fatigue may set in.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for the Playa Delfines Sunrise Visit — Cancun's most iconic public beach offering breathtaking panoramic views of the Caribbean Sea at golden hour. Arrive around 6:00–6:30 AM for the best light and a serene, crowd-free experience. A private driver can be arranged through the resort for a seamless transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Punta Nizuc for a premium guided snorkeling experience at the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef System. Explore vibrant coral formations, tropical fish, and crystal-clear turquoise waters with a certified guide. Opt for a private snorkeling charter for an exclusive, unhurried experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset cocktail hour at the rooftop or beach bar. Follow with a sophisticated dinner at a top-rated Cancun Hotel Zone restaurant known for contemporary Mexican cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Pre-sunrise light breakfast at the resort — fresh fruit, pastries, and premium coffee prepared by your butler
meals.lunch: Post-snorkel beachside lunch at a luxury waterfront restaurant near Punta Nizuc — grilled fish, shrimp aguachile, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Dinner at Porfirio's Cancun or equivalent upscale Mexican restaurant in the Hotel Zone — premium cuts, fresh seafood, and artisanal cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Book the private snorkeling charter at least 24 hours in advance through the resort concierge. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and a light cover-up for the sunrise visit. The Punta Nizuc reef is part of a protected marine area — follow all conservation guidelines.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on a full-day Isla Mujeres Day Trip by private catamaran or luxury yacht charter departing around 9:00 AM. Enjoy the scenic 30-minute crossing to the island with Champagne and light bites on deck. Arrive at the charming island and explore the colorful streets of downtown Isla Mujeres by golf cart.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Playa Norte, consistently ranked among the world's best beaches. Relax on the powdery white sand with calm, shallow turquoise waters. Enjoy snorkeling, paddleboarding, or simply lounging with a cocktail at one of the beachfront beach clubs. Optionally visit a sea turtle sanctuary on the island.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset dinner on Isla Mujeres before the return yacht journey. Board the private yacht for a magical twilight cruise back to Cancun with cocktails and canapés as the sun sets over the Caribbean.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, fresh-pressed juices, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a top beachfront restaurant on Playa Norte, Isla Mujeres — fresh grilled fish, lobster, and tropical cocktails with your feet in the sand
meals.dinner: Sunset dinner at Mango Café or Olivia Restaurant on Isla Mujeres — Mediterranean-Caribbean fusion cuisine before the return yacht journey

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the private yacht charter through the resort concierge at least 48 hours in advance. Bring cash in Mexican pesos for tips and small purchases on the island. Golf cart rentals on Isla Mujeres are a fun and easy way to explore — book in advance during peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Indulge in a luxurious morning with a world-class spa treatment at the resort's premium spa — choose from a traditional Mayan healing ritual, hot stone massage, or a rejuvenating couples' treatment. Follow with a serene yoga or meditation session on the beach at sunrise or mid-morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Full-day experience at Xel-Ha Eco Water Park, a stunning natural aquatic paradise built around a coastal lagoon. Snorkel through the lagoon's crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish, float down lazy rivers, cliff jump, and explore mangroves. The all-inclusive premium package covers gourmet food, open bar, and all activities.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a private in-suite or beachside dinner under the stars. Arrange a bespoke candlelit dining setup on the beach with a personalized menu curated by the resort's executive chef.

meals.breakfast: Lavish resort breakfast buffet or à la carte in-room dining — fresh tropical fruits, eggs to order, artisanal breads, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: All-inclusive gourmet lunch at Xel-Ha — fresh seafood, grilled meats, salads, and unlimited beverages included in the premium park package
meals.dinner: Private candlelit beachside dinner arranged by the resort concierge — customized 5-course menu with wine pairings and live acoustic music

day_by_day.notes: Book Xel-Ha tickets in advance online for the best rates and to guarantee the premium all-inclusive package. The park is approximately 75 km south of Cancun — arrange a private round-trip transfer through the resort. Wear water shoes for comfort in the lagoon.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — enjoy the resort's private beach, infinity pool, or engage in water sports such as jet skiing, parasailing, or paddleboarding arranged through the resort's water sports center. Alternatively, take a sunrise paddleboard session along the calm lagoon side of the Hotel Zone.
day_by_day.afternoon: Authentic culinary experience at El Fish Fritanga for a beloved local seafood lunch near Playa Langosta.
